findings.title: Rejected-email state is shared between controller instances
findings.body: `rejectedEmails` is a mutable array created on the controller definition, so Ember can share it across `CreateAccountController` instances rather than giving each signup modal its own list. An email rejected in one signup attempt can then remain invalid in a later attempt or another user's modal in the same page session, even if the server-side reason no longer applies. Initialize this array per controller instance.

findings.title: Concurrent matches can lose blocked-email statistics
findings.body: This increments `match_count` by reading the current value and later saving the whole record. Concurrent signup validations for the same blocked address can both read the same count and overwrite one another, so `match_count` under-reports matches. Use an atomic database increment (and update the timestamp atomically) to preserve the statistics.

findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive
findings.body: The lookup receives the submitted email unchanged, while email addresses are commonly entered with differing letter case and the blocklist's unique index also treats differently cased strings as distinct. A blocked address can therefore bypass this check simply by changing its capitalization. Normalize the address consistently when storing and looking up blocked emails.
